\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-arbitrary-prop-compactness-bpi}{cited=HowardRubin1998}{Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem and unrestricted propositional compactness}
Working over \(\mathsf{ZF}\), the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem (equivalently,
the Ultrafilter Lemma of Definition~\ref{def:ultrafilter-lemma}) is equivalent
to the following scheme: for every set \(P\) of propositional variables and
every set \(\Gamma\subseteq\operatorname{Form}(P)\), if each finite subset
of \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable, then \(\Gamma\) is satisfiable.
\end{hbtheorem}

\begin{definition}[Ultrafilter Lemma]
\label{def:ultrafilter-lemma}
The \emph{Ultrafilter Lemma} states the following.  Let \(I\) be a set and let
\(\mathcal F\subseteq\Pow(I)\) satisfy
\[
 I\in\mathcal F,\quad\varnothing\notin\mathcal F,\quad
 X,Y\in\mathcal F\Rightarrow X\cap Y\in\mathcal F,
\]
and
\[
 X\in\mathcal F\text{ and }X\subseteq Y\subseteq I
 \Rightarrow Y\in\mathcal F.
\]
Then there is \(\mathcal U\subseteq\Pow(I)\) containing \(\mathcal F\) that
satisfies the same conditions and, for every \(X\subseteq I\), contains
exactly one of \(X\) and \(I\setminus X\).  This is a metatheoretic choice
principle about families of subsets, not a formula of a first-order theory
under study.  It is strictly weaker over \(\ZF\) than the Axiom of Choice and
therefore is not a second name for that axiom.  The later filter chapter gives
the short technical terms for the two displayed families before applying this
principle.
\end{definition}

Some model-theoretic constructions use the Ultrafilter Lemma, and some cardinal
arguments use the Axiom of Choice.  Later theorems state the required principle
rather than silently treating either principle as part of pure first-order
logic.

Product principle & Every set-indexed product of nonempty sets is nonempty &
Equivalent to Choice: a point of the product is exactly a simultaneous choice
function. \\
Tychonoff, arbitrary compact spaces & Every product of compact spaces is
compact & Equivalent to Choice. \\
\addlinespace[4pt]
\multicolumn{3}{@{}l}{\textit{BPI-equivalent and restricted compactness forms}}\\*
\addlinespace[2pt]
Unrestricted propositional compactness & Every finitely satisfiable set of
formulas over an arbitrary propositional variable set is satisfiable &
Equivalent over \(\mathsf{ZF}\) to \(\mathsf{BPI}\); see
Theorem~\ref{thm:p02-arbitrary-prop-compactness-bpi}. \\
Tychonoff, compact Hausdorff spaces & Every product of compact Hausdorff spaces
is compact & Equivalent to the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem, not to full
Choice. \\
Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem / Ultrafilter Lemma & Every proper Boolean filter
extends to an ultrafilter & Choice implies it; the converse is not provable
over \(\mathsf{ZF}\) if \(\mathsf{ZF}\) is consistent
\cite{HalpernLevy1971,HowardRubin1998}. \\
